body:
Migrated from docs/agent-memory/tests.md (entry dated 2026-09-22).

`internal/trace.TestStableMetadataIncludesChangeTime` (`metadata_unix_test.go:31`) chmods 0600→0400→0600, `internal/authoritystore` `PLE-V0-003 configuration witness detects restored bytes` (`repository_metadata_test.go:33`) rewrites identical bytes then `Chtimes` the mtime back, and `internal/cem/gitauth.TestAuthorityBindingRejectsObservedNamespaceAndModeDrift/restored_modification_time` (`authority_binding_test.go:187`) does the same for an authority binding; all three then require `Ctim` to differ. Under a Linux container on ext4 at 82a113a all three FAIL ("ctime-only metadata change accepted", "restored content/mtime hid change time", "observed drift accepted") because the operations land inside one coarse ctime tick; all three PASS on Darwin/APFS. The implementations (`metadata_linux.go`, `metadata_darwin.go`) are correct — the assertion is clock-granularity dependent. Done looks like: each of the three loops or waits until `Ctim` actually advances before asserting (and `t.Skip`s if it never does), so the result does not depend on host filesystem timestamp resolution. Note the underlying product limitation the tests were written for: a restore completed within one ctime tick is genuinely invisible to the witness.
title: trace + authoritystore + gitauth: three ctime witness tests assume ctime advances between adjacent syscalls
